title: Pinch a fingertip pulse oximeter open and clip it onto a manikin's finger
instruction: Clip the blue pulse oximeter onto the manikin's outstretched index finger. Pinch the oximeter's back end to open its jaws and keep them open while you slide it over the fingertip as far as it will go (the fingertip within 2 mm of the stop inside). Then open the gripper and move it away, leaving the oximeter clipped on the finger.
context: Nursing assistants (O*NET 31-1131.00, about 1.35 million US jobs) and medical assistants (31-9092.00, about 0.8 million) take vital signs on every patient; O*NET lists recording vital signs, pulse included, as a core nursing-assistant task, and a fingertip oximeter reads pulse and oxygen saturation. The maker's instructions: open the clip, put the finger between the cushions, let it close. The clip is shut at rest (mouth 6 mm, finger 15 mm) and a grasp round the body presses its two shells together. A pinch on the 20 mm tail behind the pivot opens the mouth to 23.7 mm; the same pinch must carry the 50 g unit over the finger, 4.4 mm clear per side at the lips narrowing to 1.1 mm at the cushions' inner end, then hand the grip over to the spring. Nearest board task: TK-LXP38D (ECG lead clips set in cups on a manikin; the choice of lead is the test). Here nothing is chosen: the test is opening a sprung clip and leaving it gripping.
setup: Station table; positions in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases, x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table top. Nothing is randomised. (1) Manikin right hand and forearm, life size, rigid skin-tone plastic, fixed to the table on marked positions, lying on its little-finger edge with the thumb up and the fingers toward the robot. The index finger is outstretched and straight: 15 mm in diameter and 72 mm long with a rounded tip, level along x at y 0, its axis 75 mm up, tip at x 0.270, knuckle at x 0.342, nail facing +y. The other three fingers are curled into the palm with the thumb folded over them: a fist 95 mm (x) by 60 mm (y) by 85 mm (z), x 0.342 to 0.437, y -0.048 to +0.012. Forearm 58 mm thick, x 0.437 to 0.617. (2) Fingertip pulse oximeter, loose: a Contec CMS50D, 57 mm long, 31 mm wide, 32 mm across its two shells, 50 g with two AAA cells (the maker's figures), blue ABS. Display shell 14 g, battery shell with its cells 36 g. The shells turn on one pivot across the width, 20 mm from the back end, closed by a torsion spring. Behind the pivot is the tail: the shells stand 10 mm apart there, and each carries an added black rubber grip pad 10 x 20 x 2.5 mm at its end, 37 mm across the two pads. Ahead of the pivot is the finger chamber: 22 mm wide between the battery shell's side walls and 31 mm deep from the lips to a stop 6 mm ahead of the pivot, lined by two grey silicone cushions that are 6 mm apart at the lips and 11.7 mm apart at their inner end when shut. Pinching the grip pads together opens the chamber. Tails touching (28 degrees at the pivot; the pads' front edges, where a flat gripper pad bears, are then 31.1 mm apart): 23.7 mm at the lips, 17.2 mm at the cushions' inner end. At 16.3 degrees the two cushions are parallel and 15 mm apart, which is how they sit on this finger; the lips are then 30 mm past a fingertip that touches the stop. Spring: 0.15 N m/rad from shut; 5.2 N on each grip pad holds it fully open, and on the finger each cushion presses with about 1.9 N, against the unit's 0.49 N weight. It lies on its side (pivot upright), long axis along x, centre at (0.180, 0.000), 15.5 mm up, display shell toward +y, lips toward the manikin at x 0.2085, 61.5 mm short of the fingertip. Both arms reach the oximeter and the finger. Real build: a CMS50D with a 10 x 20 x 2.5 mm self-adhesive rubber pad on each tail, laid in a tape outline; the hand and forearm printed in skin-tone PLA to the dimensions above and screwed to the table on its marks; two pen rings round the finger, one 10 mm from its tip, the other 2 mm nearer the tip than the lips reach when the unit is pushed fully on by hand and let go (28 mm from the tip with the dimensions above). That rule and the feeler reading under scoring hold whatever the unit's inside dimensions are.
scoring: Read each control step: the poses of the oximeter's two shells, its pivot angle, the fixed finger and both grippers. Depth = how far the fingertip is past the oximeter's lips along its centre line (on the stop: 30 mm with the cushions on the finger, 28.9 fully open). In the chamber = depth 4 mm to 32.5 mm (not past the stop) with the fingertip's centre within 5 mm of the centre line. Over the finger = in the chamber at depth 10 mm or more, the oximeter's length within 20 degrees of the finger's and its display shell on the nail side (within 45 degrees). Jaws open = pivot at 22 degrees or more: mouth 20 mm or wider, front end 45.5 mm or more across the outside of the two shells (32 mm shut, 42.2 clipped on, 49.0 tails together). Slid on open = the way in was made with the jaws open, not by the fingertip spreading the cushions: counting the steps in the chamber since the fingertip last came in past the lips, its greatest depth with the jaws not open is at most 1.5 mm more than its greatest depth with them open (closing on the stop adds 1.1 mm by itself, so 1.5 allows 0.4 margin; never open there fails). Gripping = over the finger with both cushions on it: a 1 mm feeler pushed in at the lips beside the finger is stopped within 5 mm by each cushion (read from the pivot angle: within 1.8 degrees of 16.3 degrees). Let go = on every step of the last 1 s each gripper's finger zone (every point within half its finger gap plus 8 mm, and 13.5 mm across, of the 38 mm of its axis above the pad tips) is 30 mm or more from the oximeter; a gripper that cannot be read counts as not let go. Clipped on = gripping and let go, no part of the oximeter within 20 mm of the table, and through the last 1 s it has stayed gripping, moved under 2 mm and turned under 2 degrees. The highest line that holds: 1.0 (success, ends the trial after 1 s): clipped on at depth 28 mm or more (the fingertip within 2 mm of the stop) and slid on open. 0.75: clipped on, short of 28 mm or not slid on open: it holds by its own spring. 0.5: it was over the finger at depth 28 mm or more for 0.5 s at some time, and now is over the finger at depth 10 mm or more and let go, but not clipped on (not gripping, not still, or touching the table). 0.25: at some time the jaws were open for 0.5 s while every part of the oximeter was 20 mm or more above the table: pinched open and lifted by its tail, a minor first stage a held unit can earn; nothing higher is earned while held. 0: anything else. Both records last until a reset. Doing nothing: 0. A grasp round the body (jaws shut) pushed at the fingertip, or a unit laid on the hand, scores 0, or 0.25 if pinched open in the air; held open round the fingertip, or pushed home and still held, 0.25. Real trial, from the video, one photo from above and a feeler gauge: depth by the two pen rings (a ring out of sight inside the oximeter = that depth reached); jaws open by a ruler on the video frame; slid on open: after the last frame with the jaws open the lips go no more than 1.5 mm further along the finger; gripping by the feeler; display side, let go and still from photo and video.
fidelity: Rigid bodies; PhysX 240 Hz, control 20 Hz. Simplified: two shells on one hinge (0 to 28 degrees), linear spring 0.15 N m/rad from shut (real ones are preloaded). Cushions are hard stepped faces with square lips; real ones are soft and cupped; a fingertip can spread them. Pivot position, tail gap, chamber width and depth, cushion gaps, mass split and spring rate are our estimates. Fingertip rounded in 2 steps. Added: 2.5 mm grip pad on each tail. Not modelled: display, optics, readout.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Pinch the oximeter's tail, take it off the finger and lay it on its side in its tape outline: long axis along x, centre at (0.180, 0.000) m, lips toward the manikin, display shell toward +y, jaws shut. Check that the manikin hand is still screwed on its marks with the index finger level, 75 mm up, and that both pen rings can be seen. Arms at READY, grippers open; object_jitter=0.
